author: LingoLearn contributors
sourceNotice: Original lessons and exercises. Grammar stages are a teaching sequence, not calibrated proficiency certification.

explanation.en: Use am with I, is with a singular subject, and are with you or a plural subject. Put not after be to make a negative. A profession normally needs a/an in the singular.
explanation.zh: I 后用 am，单数主语后用 is，you 和复数主语后用 are。否定时在 be 后加 not。单数职业名称前通常需要 a/an。

explanation.en: Use the present simple for habits and general facts. Add -s or -es with he, she or it in positive statements. After does not, use the base form, without -s.
explanation.zh: 一般现在时表达习惯和一般事实。肯定句中，he、she、it 后的动词通常加 -s 或 -es；does not 后用动词原形。

examples: Lena walks to work every day.

questions.prompt: The shop ___ at nine every day.

explanation.en: Use do/does before the subject to ask about an action, followed by the base verb. For a sentence with be, move be before the subject instead. Who and what can themselves be subjects.
explanation.zh: 询问动作时，把 do/does 放在主语前，后面的动词用原形。句子已有 be 时，直接把 be 放到主语前。who、what 也可以作主语。

title.zh: 用现在进行时说眼前的事

explanation.en: The present continuous is am/is/are + an -ing form. It describes an action in progress or a temporary situation. Compare a regular habit with an action happening right now.
explanation.zh: 现在进行时由 am/is/are 加动词 -ing 形式构成，表示正在发生的动作或临时情况。注意区分经常做的事与此刻正在做的事。

examples: I usually cycle, but today I am walking.

questions.prompt: Look! The dog ___ in the river.
We ___ for the train right now.
I ___ a message at the moment.

title.zh: 用一般过去时叙述往事

explanation.en: Use a past form for a completed event at a finished past time. Regular verbs often end in -ed; common verbs may be irregular. After did or did not, return to the base form.
explanation.zh: 发生在已结束时间里的事件用过去式。规则动词常加 -ed，也有不规则过去式。did 或 did not 后仍用动词原形。

questions.prompt: She ___ the door five minutes ago.
I did not ___ the email yesterday.

explanation.en: Use a/an for one non-specific countable thing. Choose an before a vowel sound, not merely a vowel letter. Use the when the listener can identify which thing you mean.
explanation.zh: a/an 用于一个尚未特指的可数事物。元音音素前用 an，判断依据是发音，不只是字母。听者能确定所指事物时常用 the。

examples: I saw a dog. The dog followed me.

questions.prompt: Choose a/an for one non-specific object: I need ___ umbrella.
Refer back to the same cat: I saw a cat. ___ cat was sleeping.

explanation.en: Countable nouns have singular and plural forms. Uncountable nouns such as information, rice and advice do not normally take a/an or plural -s in these meanings. Use many with plural countable nouns and much with uncountable nouns.
explanation.zh: 可数名词有单复数。information、rice、advice 等在常见含义下不可数，不直接加 a/an 或复数 -s。many 修饰复数可数名词，much 修饰不可数名词。

examples: How many bags do you have?
We do not have much time.

title.en: At, on and in for time

explanation.en: Use at with clock times, on with days or dates, and in with months, years or longer periods. Expressions such as next Monday and last year normally have no time preposition.
explanation.zh: 钟点前用 at，星期或日期前用 on，月份、年份等较长时间前用 in。next Monday、last year 等表达前通常不用时间介词。

title.zh: 现在完成时与过去时间

explanation.en: Use have/has + past participle to connect a past event or continuing situation to now. For an event with a finished time such as yesterday, normally use the past simple. Since gives a starting point; for gives a duration.
explanation.zh: 现在完成时由 have/has 加过去分词构成，把过去的经历或持续状态与现在联系起来。yesterday 等已结束时间通常搭配一般过去时。since 表起点，for 表时长。

examples: I have lived here for five years, and I still live here.

questions.prompt: They have lived here ___ six months.

title.zh: 过去进行时与背景动作

explanation.en: Use was/were + -ing for an action in progress at a past moment. The past simple can identify an event that interrupted it. The form agrees with the subject: I/he/she was; you/we/they were.
explanation.zh: was/were 加 -ing 表示过去某时正在进行的动作。一般过去时可以表达期间突然发生的事件。注意 was 和 were 与主语的一致关系。

examples: I was cooking when the phone rang.
They were talking at ten last night.

questions.prompt: At eight last night, we ___ dinner.
While I was walking home, I ___ my neighbour.
The children ___ playing when I arrived.

title.en: Ways to talk about the future

explanation.en: Will takes a base verb. Be going to takes a base verb too, and be agrees with the subject. The present continuous can express an arrangement. After when or as soon as in a future time clause, normally use a present form rather than will.
explanation.zh: will 和 be going to 后接动词原形，后者的 be 随主语变化。现在进行时也能表达已安排的将来事项。表示将来的 when、as soon as 时间从句通常用现在时，不用 will。

examples: I will call you when I arrive.
We are meeting the team tomorrow.

questions.prompt: They ___ going to move next month.
I will text you when I ___.
We are ___ the doctor at ten tomorrow.

explanation.en: Must and can are followed by a base verb. Must not means prohibition; do not have to means there is no obligation. Have to changes with the subject and time, unlike must.
explanation.zh: must、can 后接动词原形。must not 表示禁止；do not have to 表示不必，两者含义不同。have to 会随主语、时态变化。

examples: It is optional: you do not have to attend.

questions.prompt: You must ___ a ticket before boarding.
It is forbidden. You ___ smoke here.
She ___ to wear a uniform at work.

explanation.en: Use -er or more for a comparative, not both together. Use than to introduce the second term. As ... as expresses equality. Superlatives often use the before the adjective.
explanation.zh: 比较级使用 -er 或 more，不要叠加。比较对象由 than 引出。as ... as 表示同等程度；最高级前常用 the。

examples: This bag is lighter than mine.

questions.prompt: This route is ___ than the old one.
My room is as large ___ yours.
It is the ___ building in the town.

explanation.en: A common first conditional uses if + present and will + base verb for a possible future. A second conditional uses a past form and would + base verb for an imagined present or future. Would normally belongs in the result clause, not the if clause.
explanation.zh: 常见第一条件句用 if 加现在时、主句用 will 加原形，表达可能发生的将来情况。第二条件句用过去式和 would 加原形表达现在或将来的假设。would 通常放在结果从句。

examples: If it rains, we will stay inside.
If I had a garden, I would grow tomatoes.

questions.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
If I had more time, I ___ a language.
If I ___ you, I would apologise.

title.en: Focus on the action: the passive
title.zh: 被动语态突出动作对象

explanation.en: The passive uses be + past participle. Change be to express tense and agreement. The person doing the action can be added with by, but need not be mentioned when unknown or unimportant.
explanation.zh: 被动语态由 be 加过去分词构成，be 体现时态和主谓一致。动作执行者可以用 by 引出；不清楚或不重要时可以省略。

examples: These rooms are cleaned every day.

questions.prompt: The window was broken ___ a falling branch.

explanation.en: Who refers to people, which to things, and whose introduces possession. A defining clause identifies the noun; a non-defining clause adds extra information and is separated with commas. Do not use that directly after a comma in a non-defining clause.
explanation.zh: who 指人，which 指物，whose 表所属。限制性定语从句用于确定对象；非限制性从句补充信息，用逗号隔开，逗号后通常不用 that。

examples: The woman whose bike was stolen called the police.
My car, which is ten years old, still runs well.

questions.prompt: The student ___ won the prize is here.
The writer ___ book I read lives nearby.
The cafe, ___ opened last week, is busy.
That is the tool ___ I need.

title.zh: 混合条件句的时间关系

explanation.en: A mixed conditional can connect an unreal past cause (if + had + past participle) with an unreal present result (would + base verb). A past result instead uses would have + past participle. Choose forms by the intended time, not by mechanically pairing every clause.
explanation.zh: 混合条件句可用 if 加过去完成时表达未发生的过去原因，主句用 would 加原形表达现在结果。若结果也在过去，则用 would have 加过去分词。应先判断两部分各自的时间。

examples: If I had taken that job, I would live abroad now.
If she had called earlier, we would have waited.

questions.prompt: If I had slept well, I ___ so tired now.
If they had left earlier, they ___ the train yesterday.
If he ___ the map, he would know where we are now.
If I were better at cooking, I ___ a cake for yesterday’s party.

explanation.en: After a fronted negative or restrictive expression such as never, rarely or only then, put the auxiliary before the subject. Add do/does/did when the normal sentence has no auxiliary. Not until also triggers inversion in the main clause.
explanation.zh: never、rarely、only then 等否定或限制性表达前置时，助动词放在主语前。原句没有助动词时补 do/does/did。not until 前置后，主句也用部分倒装。

examples: Never have I seen such a sky.

explanation.en: An it-cleft uses It is/was + focused information + that/who + the rest of the clause. A wh-cleft often begins with What ... and follows it with be. Keep the rest of the sentence grammatically complete after moving the focus.
explanation.zh: it 分裂句用 It is/was 加强调成分，再接 that/who 从句。wh 分裂句常用 What ... 作主语，后接 be。改变焦点后仍要保持句子结构完整。

examples: It was the noise that woke me.
What we need is more time.

questions.prompt: It was Maria ___ solved the problem.
What I need ___ a quiet room.
It was yesterday ___ we received the news.

choices: It was the wind that broke the branch.
It the wind was broke the branch.
It was the wind what break the branch.

explanation.en: A participle clause normally shares its understood subject with the main clause. An -ing form often has active meaning; a past participle often has passive meaning. Having + past participle marks an action completed before the main action.
explanation.zh: 分词结构的隐含主语通常应与主句主语一致。-ing 形式常表主动，过去分词常表被动。having 加过去分词表示先于主句完成的动作。

examples: Having checked the address, I posted the letter.
Built of stone, the house stays cool.

questions.prompt: ___ the report, she sent it to her manager.
___ by the noise, the baby woke up.
Choose the sentence with a clear shared subject.
choices: Walking home, I noticed the stars.
Walking home, the stars looked bright.
Walking home, the sky was dark.

questions.prompt: The samples, ___ at low temperature, remained stable.

explanation.en: Reporting passives separate a reported claim from the writer’s own assertion: It is believed that ... or The person is believed to ... . Use to have + past participle when the reported action happened before the reporting time.
explanation.zh: It is believed that ... 或主语加 is believed to ... 用于表明这是他人的说法。若被报道的动作早于报道时点，不定式可用 to have 加过去分词。

examples: The painting is believed to be genuine.
The suspect is reported to have left yesterday.

questions.prompt: He is reported ___ the country last week.
It is said ___ the building is unsafe.
The documents are thought to have been ___.

explanation.en: Use modal + have + past participle to reason about a past event. Must have expresses a strong positive inference; cannot have expresses a strong negative inference. Might have leaves the possibility open. Should have can express an unmet expectation or criticism.
explanation.zh: 情态动词加 have 加过去分词可推测过去。must have 表强肯定推断，cannot have 表强否定推断，might have 表可能。should have 也可表示未实现的期待或批评。

examples: The floor is wet; someone must have spilled water.
You should have told me earlier.

questions.prompt: It is possible that he forgot. He ___ forgotten.
They cannot have ___ here: the door was locked.

title.zh: 建议要求中的虚拟语气

explanation.en: After expressions such as recommend that or essential that, formal English can use a base-form subjunctive: she be, he attend. It does not add third-person -s. Should + base verb is another common pattern, especially in British English.
explanation.zh: recommend that、essential that 等后面，正式英语可用动词原形的虚拟语气，例如 she be、he attend，不加第三人称 -s。英式英语也常用 should 加原形。

examples: They recommended that he attend the meeting.
It is essential that everyone be informed.

questions.prompt: Use the base-form subjunctive: They insist that she ___ present.
Use the base-form subjunctive: I suggest that he ___ again.
It is vital that the file should ___ backed up.

choices: They asked that he does not discloses the result.
They asked that he not disclosed the result.
They asked that he not disclose the result.

explanation.en: Although introduces a clause with a subject and verb. Despite normally takes a noun or -ing form, or the phrase the fact that + clause. However is a linking adverb; it does not by itself join two independent clauses with only a comma.
explanation.zh: although 后接有主语和谓语的从句。despite 后常接名词或 -ing 形式，也可接 the fact that 从句。however 是连接副词，不能仅靠它和一个逗号拼接两个独立分句。

examples: Although it was cold, we went outside.
It was cold. However, we went outside.

questions.prompt: ___ it was raining, they kept working.
Despite ___ tired, she finished the task.

choices: The plan was costly however it worked.
The plan was costly; however, it worked.
The plan was costly, however it worked.

explanation.en: Use 是 to connect a person with a noun describing identity. Negate it with 不是. An adjective predicate such as 很忙 usually does not need 是.
explanation.zh: “是”连接人物和身份名词；否定用“不是”。“很忙”这类形容词谓语通常不需要“是”。

questions.prompt: 用“是”介绍她的职业：她___一名护士。
不表示强调，只用形容词作谓语，哪句合适？

explanation.en: 有 expresses possession or existence. Its ordinary negative is 没有, not 不有. A location can come first to introduce something present there.
explanation.zh: “有”表达拥有或存在，通常用“没有”否定。地点放在前面时，可以介绍那里有什么。

explanation.en: Add 吗 to a statement to form a yes/no question. Do not normally add 吗 to an A-not-A question such as 是不是. Questions with 谁 or 什么 already contain a question word.
explanation.zh: 在陈述句末加“吗”可构成是非问。“是不是”等正反问一般不再加“吗”；“谁、什么”等疑问词也已表达提问。

questions.prompt: 用“吗”构成普通的是非问：你会说中文___？
“你叫什么名字？”里的疑问词是___。

explanation.en: A number normally comes before a measure word and a noun: 三本书. Common pairings include 本 for books, 张 for flat sheets and 把 for many handled objects such as umbrellas. These pairings need to be learned with the noun.
explanation.zh: 数词、量词、名词通常依次排列，如“三本书”。书常用“本”，纸常用“张”，伞常用“把”。学习名词时最好一起记常用量词。

explanation.en: 了 after a verb can mark a completed action; it is not a general past-tense ending. 没有 negates a completed action and normally removes this verb-final 了. Sentence-final 了 can instead signal a changed situation.
explanation.zh: 动词后的“了”可以表示动作完成，并不是通用的过去时词尾。用“没有”否定动作完成时，通常去掉这一“了”。句末“了”也可表示情况变化。

questions.prompt: 请选择表示完成的句子。
否定“他吃了早饭”所说的已完成动作，应选哪句？

explanation.en: Verb + 过 often expresses experience before now. 没有 + verb + 过 negates that experience. Compare 去过 (have been before) with 去了 (went, in a particular event).
explanation.zh: 动词加“过”常表示曾经有过某种经历。“没有”加动词加“过”表示没有这种经历。“去过”重在经历，“去了”重在一次具体事件。

questions.prompt: 她从来没有吃___这种水果。

explanation.en: The common comparison pattern is A 比 B + adjective. Do not add 很 before that adjective in a simple 比 comparison. You can add 一点儿 or a measured difference after the adjective.
explanation.zh: 常见结构是“A 比 B 加形容词”。简单的“比”字句中，形容词前通常不加“很”；形容词后可加“一点儿”或具体差量。

examples: 这本书比那本书贵一点儿。

explanation.en: 把 places a known object before the verb and often highlights how it is affected. The verb usually needs a result, direction or other completion information. Negatives and modals normally go before 把.
explanation.zh: “把”把已知对象放到动词前，突出它受到的处理。动词后通常要有结果、趋向等补充信息。否定词、能愿动词一般放在“把”前。

explanation.en: 被 introduces a passive relationship: the subject receives the action. The agent can follow 被 or be omitted. The predicate usually describes an effect or result rather than a bare action.
explanation.zh: “被”字句的主语是动作的承受者。“被”后可写动作执行者，也可省略；谓语通常说明受到的影响或结果。

examples: 这个问题已经被解决了。

questions.prompt: 在“他被老师表扬了”中，动作执行者是___。

explanation.en: 虽然 introduces a concession, and 但是 or 可是 can introduce a contrasting result. 即使 expresses a hypothetical concession and often pairs with 也. Distinguish an established fact from an imagined condition.
explanation.zh: “虽然”引出让步事实，“但是、可是”等引出转折结果。“即使”常表达假设性让步，与“也”呼应，应区分已有事实和假设条件。

examples: 虽然很累，但是她没有放弃。
即使下雨，我们也会出发。

questions.prompt: 即使遇到困难，我们___不会放弃。

explanation.en: 无论 and 不管 introduce a range of conditions, often with question words or alternatives. 都 or 也 in the following clause says the result holds across them. 只有 ... 才 instead states a necessary condition.
explanation.zh: “无论、不管”常与疑问词或选择形式搭配，表示任一条件；后面的“都、也”说明结果不受这些条件影响。“只有……才……”则强调必要条件。

examples: 无论你在哪里，我都会支持你。
只有认真检查，才能发现问题。

questions.prompt: 无论发生什么，我___会帮你。
___你去不去，活动都会照常举行。
只有按时提交，___能参加评选。

explanation.en: Word order changes the scope of negation. 不都 means not all; 都不 means none of the group do the action. 并不是 ... 都 ... explicitly rejects a generalization without asserting that every member fails.
explanation.zh: 否定词的位置会改变范围。“不都”是否定全部成立，即并非每个都如此；“都不”则对所有成员否定。“并不是……都……”用于否定一概而论。

examples: 这些书不都适合初学者。

questions.prompt: 请选择表示“并非所有”的句子。
choices: 并不是所有建议都可行。

explanation.en: In a polite noun sentence, place です after the noun. A common negative is ではありません. Do not attach です directly to a polite verb form such as 行きます.
explanation.zh: 礼貌体名词句在名词后用です，常见否定形式为ではありません。行きます等礼貌体动词后不再直接加です。

examples: 田中さんは先生ではありません。

questions.prompt: 自然な文を選んでください。

explanation.en: は introduces a topic; it is pronounced wa as a particle. の links a possessor or modifier to a noun. A question can keep the topic and replace the unknown identity with だれ or 何.
explanation.zh: 助词は提示话题，读作 wa。の连接所属者或修饰语与名词。提问身份时可以保留话题，用だれ、何表示未知内容。

examples: これは私のかばんです。

questions.prompt: これは田中さん___本です。

explanation.en: を marks a direct object. で marks the place where an action occurs. に commonly marks the destination or the location of existence, so existence and action locations use different patterns.
explanation.zh: を标记直接宾语。で表示动作发生的地点；に常表示目的地或存在的位置，要区分动作地点与存在地点。

examples: 図書館で本を読みます。
机の上に本があります。

title.zh: ます体的现在、过去和否定

explanation.en: Polite verbs use ます, ません, ました and ませんでした for non-past positive, non-past negative, past positive and past negative. Keep the verb stem before these endings.
explanation.zh: 礼貌体动词的非过去肯定、否定、过去肯定、过去否定分别用ます、ません、ました、ませんでした，前接相应词干。

examples: 昨日は働きませんでした。

questions.prompt: 「行きます」の否定はどれですか。

title.en: Actions in progress with ている

explanation.en: The て-form + いる/います can describe an ongoing action. Some verbs instead express a resulting state, as in 結婚しています. First form the て-form correctly: 読む becomes 読んで.
explanation.zh: 动词て形加いる/います可表示动作进行。有些动词表示结果状态，如結婚しています。先注意て形变化，例如読む变为読んで。

title.en: Explain reasons with から and ので

explanation.en: から and ので introduce reasons. Before ので, a noun or な-adjective normally uses な: 学生なので、静かなので. An い-adjective keeps its い. Polite forms can also be followed by から.
explanation.zh: から和ので表示原因。名词、な形容词接ので时通常加な，如学生なので、静かなので；い形容词保留い。礼貌体后也可接から。

examples: 暑いから、窓を開けます。

questions.prompt: 静か___ので、ここで勉強します。
今日は寒い___、上着を着ます。
学生___ので、割引があります。

title.zh: たことがある表达经历

explanation.en: Use the plain past form + ことがある to describe an experience. A negative such as ことがありません means the experience has not happened. This differs from the past of a particular event.
explanation.zh: 动词普通体过去式加ことがある表示曾有过某种经历。ことがありません表示没有这种经历，与叙述一次具体过去事件不同。

examples: 京都に行ったことがあります。
すしを作ったことはありません。

questions.prompt: 日本に___ことがあります。
この映画を___ことがあります。
「経験がない」という意味はどれですか。
choices: 行ったことがありません。

questions.prompt: 富士山に登ったこと___ありますか。

title.en: Compare with より and ほう

explanation.en: A は B より adjective says A has more of a quality than B. B より A のほうが adjective focuses on A. In a comparison question, どちら asks which of two alternatives.
explanation.zh: AはBより加形容词表示A比B更具有某种性质。BよりAのほうが加形容词也可表达比较。どちら用于询问两个选项中的哪一个。

examples: 電車はバスより速いです。
夏より冬のほうが好きです。

questions.prompt: 紅茶とコーヒーと、___が好きですか。
冬___夏のほうが暑いです。

explanation.en: 限り can mean as long as or within the limits of something. 知っている限り means as far as one knows; できる限り means as much as possible. The form and context determine which boundary is expressed.
explanation.zh: 限り可表示“只要……就……”或“在……范围内”。知っている限り表示“据我所知”，できる限り表示“尽可能”，需结合前接形式和语境判断范围。

examples: 私が知っている限り、店は開いています。
できる限り手伝います。

questions.prompt: 私が知っている___、彼はまだ来ていません。
できる___早く返事をください。
元気である___、働き続けたいです。
「知っている限り」は何を限定しますか。

title.zh: わけではない表示部分否定

explanation.en: わけではない can reject an inference or an overgeneralization. 必ずしも ... わけではない means not necessarily. It does not always mean that the opposite is completely true.
explanation.zh: わけではない可否定某种推论或一概而论。必ずしも……わけではない表示“未必、并非一定”，不能一律理解成完全相反的结论。

examples: 高い物が必ずしも良いわけではありません。
嫌いなわけではないですが、今日は食べません。

questions.prompt: 全部分かった___ではありません。
必ずしも高い物が良いわけでは___。
「嫌いなわけではない」はどんな意味ですか。
choices: 嫌いだという推測を否定する

questions.prompt: 全員が賛成した___ではありません。

title.zh: にもかかわらず表达逆接

explanation.en: にもかかわらず links an established circumstance with an unexpected result and is common in formal writing. It can follow a plain-form clause or a noun. Keep it distinct from a reason-result connection.
explanation.zh: にもかかわらず把已知情况与出乎预期的结果连接起来，常用于正式表达，可接普通体从句或名词，要与因果关系区分。

examples: 雨にもかかわらず、大勢の人が集まりました。
十分準備したにもかかわらず、緊張しました。

questions.prompt: 雨___かかわらず、試合は続きました。
努力したにもかかわらず、結果が出ませんでした。この文は何を表しますか。
choices: 単純な原因と当然の結果

questions.prompt: 休日にも___、彼は出勤しました。
「準備したにもかかわらず」に続く自然な内容はどれですか。
choices: 準備したことそのものです。

title.zh: ざるを得ない表达不得不

explanation.en: ざるを得ない means that circumstances leave no acceptable alternative. It attaches to the negative stem: 行かない becomes 行かざるを得ない. する is irregular and becomes せざるを得ない.
explanation.zh: ざるを得ない表示因情况所迫而不得不做。接动词未然形，如行かない变为行かざるを得ない。する较特殊，要用せざるを得ない。

examples: 予定を変更せざるを得ません。
証拠を認めざるを得ません。

questions.prompt: 計画を変更___ざるを得ません。
この事実を認め___を得ません。
「行く」を使ってください。行か___を得ません。
「ざるを得ない」の意味に近いのはどれですか。
choices: 絶対にしてはいけない
ほかに選択肢がなく、しなければならない

explanation.en: In polite everyday noun sentences, use 이에요 after a final consonant and 예요 after a vowel. To negate identity, use noun + 이/가 아니에요 rather than attaching a negative verb ending to the noun.
explanation.zh: 日常礼貌体名词句中，有收音时用이에요，无收音时用예요。否定身份用名词加이/가 아니에요，不直接给名词加动词否定词尾。

explanation.en: 은/는 marks a topic and can also signal contrast. Use 은 after a final consonant and 는 after a vowel. It is different from the object marker 을/를.
explanation.zh: 은/는提示话题，也可表达对比。有收音时用은，无收音时用는；不要与宾格助词을/를混淆。

explanation.en: 을/를 marks the direct object of an action. Use 을 after a consonant and 를 after a vowel. Korean often places the verb at the end of a simple clause.
explanation.zh: 을/를标记动作的直接对象。有收音时用을，无收音时用를。韩语简单句的动词常位于句末。

title.en: Where you are and where you act

explanation.en: 에 marks a location with 있다/없다 and commonly a destination with 가다/오다. 에서 marks where an action such as studying or eating takes place. The verb helps determine which marker is needed.
explanation.zh: 에用于있다/없다的存在地点，也常表示가다/오다的目的地。에서表示学习、吃饭等动作发生的地点，要结合动词选择。

questions.prompt: 목적지를 나타내는 조사를 고르세요. 내일 학교___ 가요.

explanation.en: Add -고 있다 to a verb stem to describe an action in progress. Use 있어요 for a polite current action and 있었어요 for an action in progress in the past. Stative uses and clothing expressions have their own patterns.
explanation.zh: 动词词干加고 있다可表示正在进行的动作。礼貌体现在用있어요，过去进行用있었어요。状态和穿戴表达还可能有各自的用法。

explanation.en: -아서/-어서 connects a cause to a result. 하다 commonly becomes 해서. In a simple cause-result sentence, the final predicate carries the main tense. For commands and suggestions, -(으)니까 is often the more appropriate reason connector.
explanation.zh: 아서/어서把原因连接到结果，하다常变为해서。简单因果句的主要时态通常在句末谓语体现。命令、建议前的原因表达常用(으)니까。

explanation.en: 보다 marks the comparison standard, with 더 often expressing more. The standard may appear before or after the topic. 가장 or 제일 can mark a superlative within a group.
explanation.zh: 보다标记比较基准，더常表示“更”。比较基准可放在话题前后。가장、제일可表达某一范围里的最高程度。

questions.prompt: 두 가방의 크기를 비교하세요. 이 가방이 저 가방보다 ___ 커요.
「A보다 B가 더 커요」에서 더 큰 것은 무엇인가요?

title.en: Say what you want to do

explanation.en: Verb stem + -고 싶다 expresses the speaker’s wish to do something. Use -고 싶어요 politely. For someone else’s observed wishes, -고 싶어 하다 is a common pattern. A noun desire can instead use 갖고 싶다 or 원하다 as appropriate.
explanation.zh: 动词词干加고 싶다表达想做某事，礼貌体用고 싶어요。描述别人表现出的愿望时常用고 싶어 하다。希望拥有物品时可根据语境用갖고 싶다等。

questions.prompt: 말하는 사람의 소망을 나타내세요. 저는 물을 마시고 ___.

explanation.en: -더라도 presents a condition that will not change the result. It often translates as even if. Distinguish this hypothetical concession from simply giving a cause.
explanation.zh: 더라도表示某种条件即使成立，后面的结果也不改变，常译为“即使”。要与单纯说明原因区分。

questions.prompt: 양보 조건을 나타내세요. 바쁘___ 연락해 주세요.
양보 조건을 나타내세요. 늦___ 꼭 와 주세요.

explanation.en: 반면에 contrasts two sides. An action verb commonly takes -는 반면에; a descriptive verb uses an appropriate attributive form, such as 비싼 반면에. The contrast may concern the same subject or two subjects.
explanation.zh: 반면에突出两方面的对照。动作动词常接는 반면에；描述词采用相应定语形式，如비싼 반면에。可以比较同一对象的两面，也可以比较两个对象。

examples: 이 제품은 비싼 반면에 품질이 좋아요.
형은 운동을 좋아하는 반면에 저는 독서를 좋아해요.

questions.prompt: 두 사람의 차이를 대조하세요. 그는 아침에 일하는 ___ 저는 밤에 일해요.
「장점이 있는 반면에 단점도 있다」는 무엇을 나타내나요?
「좋아하다」를 알맞게 바꾸세요. 운동을 ___ 반면에 독서는 싫어해요.

explanation.en: -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 means there is no alternative but to do something. Add -을 after most consonant-ending stems and -ㄹ after vowel-ending stems. 밖에 in this meaning requires a negative predicate such as 없다.
explanation.zh: (으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다表示除了这样做没有其他选择。多数有收音词干后加을，无收音后加ㄹ；这里的밖에要与없다等否定形式呼应。

title.zh: 는 것은 아니다表示部分否定

explanation.en: -는 것은 아니다 can reject a generalization or inference. 모두 ... 것은 아니다 means not everyone/not everything necessarily fits the claim; 아무도 ... 않다 instead denies it for everyone. Read the scope carefully.
explanation.zh: 는 것은 아니다可否定概括或推论。모두……것은 아니다常表示并非所有都如此；아무도……않다则对所有人否定。理解时要仔细判断否定范围。

questions.prompt: 「모두가 동의하는 것은 아니다」와 가까운 뜻은 무엇인가요?

explanation.en: Ser commonly expresses identity or a characteristic; estar commonly expresses location or a current state. The adjective meaning and context can change the choice. Learn the forms with the subject rather than treating the verbs as interchangeable.
explanation.zh: ser常表达身份、特征，estar常表达位置或当前状态。形容词含义和语境也会影响选择，应结合主语学习变位，不要把两者当成可以互换。

questions.prompt: La biblioteca ___ al lado del parque.

explanation.en: Regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs change their endings for the subject. Yo often ends in -o. Nosotros uses -amos, -emos or -imos. Subject pronouns can be omitted when the verb and context identify the person.
explanation.zh: 规则-ar、-er、-ir动词根据主语改变词尾。yo常对应-o；nosotros分别对应-amos、-emos、-imos。主语明确时，主语代词可以省略。

title.zh: 名词、冠词与形容词的一致

explanation.en: Articles and many adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number. Not every noun ending predicts gender, so learn the article with the noun. Adjectives ending in -e often keep the same gender form but still change for number.
explanation.zh: 冠词和许多形容词与名词保持性数一致。不能只靠词尾判断所有名词的性，建议连同冠词一起学习。-e结尾的形容词常不分性，但仍有数的变化。

explanation.en: Use dónde for place, cuándo for time, quién for a person and cuánto for quantity. Direct written questions have both opening and closing question marks. Question words carry written accents.
explanation.zh: dónde问地点，cuándo问时间，quién问人物，cuánto问数量。书面直接疑问句前后都使用问号，疑问词带重音符号。

questions.prompt: ¿___ empieza la clase? — A las nueve.

title.zh: 简单过去时与过去未完成时

explanation.en: The preterite presents a past event as complete. The imperfect commonly sets a background or describes a repeated past habit. Context and the speaker’s viewpoint matter; a time word alone does not mechanically determine the tense.
explanation.zh: 简单过去时把过去事件作为完成的整体叙述；过去未完成时常表达背景或过去习惯。语境与叙述视角很重要，不能机械地只凭一个时间词选时态。

examples: De niña, jugaba en este parque todos los días.

questions.prompt: Usa el pretérito: ayer yo ___ un libro.
Describe un hábito de la infancia: todos los días ___ al parque.
Usa el imperfecto de ser: cuando ___ niña, vivía aquí.
Usa el pretérito de llegar: ellos ___ anoche.

title.en: Purpose and cause: para and por

explanation.en: Para commonly marks purpose, a recipient or a deadline. Por commonly gives a reason, route or exchange. These are starting patterns, not a universal translation rule for the English word for.
explanation.zh: para常表示目的、接收者或期限；por常表示原因、途经或交换。这些是基本用法，不能把英语for全部机械对应到同一个介词。

questions.prompt: Indica el destinatario: este regalo es ___ ti.

title.en: Compare with más, menos and tan

explanation.en: Use más/menos + adjective + que for a difference. Use tan + adjective + como for equality. Bueno and malo have common irregular comparatives mejor and peor; normally avoid más mejor.
explanation.zh: 不同程度的比较用más/menos加形容词加que；同等比较用tan加形容词加como。bueno、malo常用不规则比较级mejor、peor，通常不用más mejor。

examples: Este tren es más rápido que aquel.
Mi habitación es tan grande como la tuya.

questions.prompt: Este tren es más rápido ___ aquel.
Esta opción es ___ que la otra.
Mi casa es menos grande ___ la tuya.

title.zh: 直接宾语代词的位置与一致

explanation.en: Lo, la, los and las commonly replace direct objects and agree with the replaced noun. They normally precede a conjugated verb. With an infinitive, they can attach to its end; some verbal phrases allow placement before the conjugated verb too.
explanation.zh: lo、la、los、las常替代直接宾语，并与所指名词保持性数一致。通常放在变位动词前，也可以连接在不定式后面；部分动词短语允许两种位置。

examples: Voy a leerlo. / Lo voy a leer.

questions.prompt: Una colocación correcta con infinitivo es ___.

title.zh: 愿望从句与现在虚拟式

explanation.en: A wish or recommendation about a different subject often takes que + subjunctive. With the same subject, an infinitive is common: quiero ir. A factual statement with sé que normally takes the indicative.
explanation.zh: 愿望、建议涉及另一个主语时，常用que加虚拟式；主语相同时常用不定式，如quiero ir。sé que等表达已知事实时通常用直陈式。

questions.prompt: Con el mismo sujeto: quiero ___ pronto.

explanation.en: For an unreal or hypothetical present condition, a common pattern is si + imperfect subjunctive followed by a conditional result. For an unreal past condition, use si + pluperfect subjunctive and a conditional perfect result.
explanation.zh: 非现实或假设的现在条件，常用si加过去未完成虚拟式，结果用条件式。过去未实现的条件常用si加过去完成虚拟式，结果用复合条件式。

questions.prompt: Usa una condición irreal del pasado: si ___ antes, habría visto a Ana.

explanation.en: In passive se constructions, the verb agrees with the grammatical subject: se venden pisos. In impersonal se constructions with a personal a, the verb is singular: se busca a los responsables. Identify the structure before choosing agreement.
explanation.zh: 自复被动结构里，动词与语法主语一致，如se venden pisos。带人称前置词a的无人称结构使用单数动词，如se busca a los responsables。先识别结构，再决定一致关系。

questions.prompt: En pasiva refleja: se ___ las entradas por internet.

title.zh: 因果、让步和目的连接词

explanation.en: Aunque can introduce a concession; porque gives a cause. Para que with a different subject introduces a purpose and normally takes the subjunctive. Sin embargo links a contrast between statements and needs appropriate punctuation.
explanation.zh: aunque引出让步，porque说明原因。para que涉及不同主语的目的时通常接虚拟式。sin embargo连接转折关系，需要合适的标点。

examples: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
Es caro; sin embargo, es útil.

questions.prompt: Te lo explico para que lo ___.

choices: Trabajo sin embargo mis hijos estudiar.
Trabajo para que mis hijos estudien.
Trabajo porque que mis hijos estudian.

explanation.en: Place 在 before a location word to say where someone or something is: 我在家. To say where an action happens, put 在 + place before the verb: 她在图书馆看书. Negate with 不在. Use 是 for identity, not location.
explanation.zh: “在”加处所词表示所在位置：我在家。表示动作发生的地点时，“在＋处所”放在动词前：她在图书馆看书。否定用“不在”。表身份用“是”，二者分工不同。

questions.prompt: 表示动作发生的地点，哪句正确？

explanation.en: Put the length of time after the verb: 我学了三年汉语. When the object is a noun, repeat the verb or attach it with 的: 他学汉语学了三年 / 我看了两个小时的书. Negate with 没（有）: 我没等多久.
explanation.zh: 时长放在动词后：我学了三年汉语。宾语是名词时可重复动词（他学汉语学了三年），或用“的”连接（我看了两个小时的书）。否定用“没（有）”：我没等多久。

questions.prompt: 带名词宾语又带时长，哪种说法自然？
choices: 他工作八个小时了公司。
他在公司工作了八个小时。
他八个小时工作在公司。

explanation.en: い-adjectives end in い and inflect by themselves: 高い → 高くない → 高かった. な-adjectives keep the stem and need な before a noun (静かな町); in the predicate they take です or だ: この町は静かです.
explanation.zh: い形容词以“い”结尾，自身变形：高い→高くない→高かった。な形容词修饰名词时接“な”（静かな町），作谓语时用“です／だ”：この町は静かです。

examples: この本はおもしろいです。
静かな公園で休みます。

questions.prompt: 否定：この店は高く___です。

explanation.en: The potential form says that someone can do something. Ru-verbs change る to られる: 食べる → 食べられる. U-verbs move to the e-row plus る: 読む → 読める. Two verbs are fixed: する → できる, 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が: 日本語が話せます.
explanation.zh: 可能形表示“会、能”。一段动词把“る”换成“られる”：食べる→食べられる。五段动词变成え段加“る”：読む→読める。特殊：する→できる、来る→来られる。对象常用“が”：日本語が話せます。

examples: 彼は日本語が話せます。
この漢字は読めますか。

title.en: Not doing with 안 and 못

explanation.en: 안 before a verb says someone does not do something by choice: 저는 안 먹어요. 못 says they cannot do it: 시간이 없어서 못 가요. Put 안 or 못 directly in front of the verb; the polite 아/어요 ending stays the same.
explanation.zh: 动词前加“안”表示主观不做：저는 안 먹어요（我不吃）。加“못”表示不能：시간이 없어서 못 가요（没时间，去不了）。안、못 直接放在动词前，词尾仍用礼貌的 아/어요。

questions.prompt: 저는 커피를 ___ 마셔요.（自己决定不喝）
동생은 매운 음식을 ___ 먹어요.（弟弟吃不了辣）

explanation.en: Attach ㄹ 거예요 after a vowel and 을 거예요 after a consonant to talk about a plan or a guess: 갈 거예요 / 먹을 거예요. It also works for adjectives and guesses about the future: 좋을 거예요. It describes intention or expectation, not a fixed timetable.
explanation.zh: 元音后接“ㄹ 거예요”，辅音后接“을 거예요”，表示打算或推测：갈 거예요／먹을 거예요。形容词同样可用：좋을 거예요。它表示将来的打算或推测，不是固定日程。

explanation.en: With gustar the thing liked is the subject: me gusta el libro, me gustan los libros. Put me, te, le, nos, os or les in front to say who likes it; use gusta for a singular thing or an action and gustan for plurals. Negate with no: no me gusta.
explanation.zh: gustar 的主语是“被喜欢的事物”：me gusta el libro／me gustan los libros。前面用 me/te/le/nos/os/les 表示“谁喜欢”；单数事物或动作用 gusta，复数用 gustan。否定加 no：no me gusta。

explanation.en: Reflexive verbs describe actions done to oneself, and the pronoun matches the subject: me despierto, te levantas, se ducha. The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or attaches to an infinitive: voy a acostarme. They can also mark a change of state: me enfermé.
explanation.zh: 自复动词表示动作回到自身，代词随主语变化：me despierto／te levantas／se ducha。代词放在变位动词之前，或附在不定式之后：voy a acostarme。也可表示状态变化：me enfermé。

title.en: The more…the more with 越…越…

explanation.en: 越…越… links two degrees that grow together: the first clause gives the condition and the second shows the result deepening with it. One adjective can repeat around the verb: 越学越有意思. With two different actors or aspects, use two 越 clauses: 雨越下越大. It marks a proportional tendency, not a fixed amount.
explanation.zh: “越…越…”连接两个同向变化的程度：前一分句给出条件，后一分句表示随之加深的结果。同一动词可复现：越学越有意思。主体或方面不同时用两个“越”分句：雨越下越大。它表示正比趋势，不表示固定数量。

questions.prompt: 两个主体都在变化，哪句自然？

title.en: The more…the more with ば〜ほど

explanation.en: Attach the conditional ば to a verb or adjective, then repeat the plain form with ほど: 読めば読むほど means the more you read. The pattern links two degrees that grow together: 練習すればするほど上手になる. It marks a proportional tendency, not a fixed amount.
explanation.zh: 动词或形容词接假定形「ば」，再重复原形加「ほど」：読めば読むほど 意为“越读越……”。「〜ば〜ほど」连接两个同向变化的程度：練習すればするほど上手になる。它表示正比趋势，不是固定数量。

examples: 考えれば考えるほど分からなくなる。
見れば見るほど美しい。

questions.prompt: 練習すれば___ほど上手になります。
値段が高ければ高い___品質がいいとは限らない。

explanation.en: -(으)ㄹ수록 links a growing condition to a growing result: 갈수록 means the more it goes on. After a consonant use 을수록 (먹을수록); after a vowel use ㄹ수록 (볼수록). The verb or adjective does not repeat: 볼수록 좋아요. It marks a proportional tendency, not a fixed amount.
explanation.zh: -(으)ㄹ수록 连接递增的条件与递增的结果：갈수록 意为“越来越……”。辅音后接 을수록（먹을수록），元音后接 ㄹ수록（볼수록）。动词不重复：볼수록 좋아요。它表示正比趋势，不是固定数量。

explanation.en: Cuanto más X, más Y links two degrees that grow together: cuanto más estudias, más aprendes. The word after cuanto agrees with what it modifies: cuanta más agua, más sano. Mientras más is an informal variant. It marks a proportional tendency, not a fixed amount.
explanation.zh: cuanto más X, más Y 连接两个同步变化的程度：cuanto más estudias, más aprendes（越学越会）。cuanto 后的词要与其修饰对象配合：cuanta más agua。mientras más 是口语变体。它表示正比趋势，不是固定数量。

examples: Cuanto más leo, más quiero leer.

questions.prompt: ___ más agua bebes, mejor te sientes.

title.en: Can and may with 会 and 可以
title.zh: 用“会”和“可以”表达能力与许可

explanation.en: 会 expresses a learned skill: 我会游泳 means I can swim. 可以 expresses permission or possibility: 这里可以停车 means you may park here. For future ability use 会: 明天我会来. The negatives are 不会 and 不可以.
explanation.zh: “会”表示学会的技能：我会游泳。“可以”表示许可或可能：这里可以停车。将来的能力也用“会”：明天我会来。否定式是“不会”和“不可以”。

title.en: Ask and allow with 〜てもいい

explanation.en: The て-form plus もいい asks or gives permission: 写真を撮ってもいいですか means May I take photos? Answer yes with いいですよ or refuse with だめです. For a clear rule use 〜てはいけません: ここで泳いではいけません means you must not swim here.
explanation.zh: 动词て形加「もいい」用于请求或给予许可：写真を撮ってもいいですか（可以拍照吗？）。肯定回答用「いいですよ」，否定用「だめです」。表示禁止用「〜てはいけません」：ここで泳いではいけません。

examples: ここに座ってもいいです。
危ないので、触ってはいけません。

questions.prompt: 写真を撮って___いいですか。

choices: ここで食べてもいいです。
ここ食べてもいいです。
ここが食べてもいいです。

explanation.en: -아/어도 돼요 asks or gives permission: 사진을 찍어도 돼요? means May I take photos? For a rule of prohibition use -면 안 돼요: 여기서 수영하면 안 돼요 means you must not swim here. After ㅏ/ㅗ vowels use -아도; elsewhere use -어도.
explanation.zh: -아/어도 돼요 用于请求或给予许可：사진을 찍어도 돼요?（可以拍照吗？）。表示禁止用 -면 안 돼요：여기서 수영하면 안 돼요。ㅏ/ㅗ 元音后接 -아도，其余接 -어도。

explanation.en: Poder + infinitive expresses ability or permission: puedo nadar means I can swim and ¿puedo entrar? asks May I come in? It is irregular in the present: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden. The verb after poder stays in the infinitive.
explanation.zh: poder + 原形动词表示能力或许可：puedo nadar（我会游泳）；¿puedo entrar?（我可以进来吗？）。现在时变位不规则：puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden。poder 后的动词保持原形。

questions.prompt: Después de poder, el verbo va en ___.

title.en: Purpose with 为了 and 来/去
title.zh: 用“为了”和“来/去”表达目的

explanation.en: 为了 introduces a purpose: 为了健康，他每天跑步 means he runs every day for his health. The purpose can also come second: 他每天跑步是为了健康. A movement verb with 来 or 去 can introduce the goal: 我来北京学习 means I came to Beijing to study.
explanation.zh: “为了”引出目的：为了健康，他每天跑步。目的分句也可后置：他每天跑步是为了健康。位移动词后加“来/去”也可引出目的：我来北京学习。

examples: 为了提高成绩，她每天复习。

title.en: Purpose with ために and ように
title.zh: 用「ために/ように」表达目的

explanation.en: Dictionary form plus ために marks a purpose the subject controls: 日本語を勉強するために日本へ来ました means I came to Japan to study Japanese. Use ように after verbs the subject cannot fully control: 見えるように前に座ります means I sat in front so that I could see. A noun takes のために.
explanation.zh: 动词辞书形加「ために」表示主体可控的目的：日本語を勉強するために日本へ来ました。难以自控的动词用「ように」：見えるように前に座ります。名词用「のために」。

examples: 健康のために毎日歩いています。
忘れないようにメモしました。

questions.prompt: 日本語を勉強する___日本へ来ました。
聞こえる___大きな声で話します。

choices: 忘れないようにメモしました。
忘れないためにメモしました。
忘れなくてようにメモしました。

explanation.en: -(으)려고 attaches to a verb stem to mark intention or purpose: 한국어를 배우려고 한국에 왔어요 means I came to Korea to learn Korean. After a consonant use 으려고; after a vowel use 려고. It cannot combine with a past-tense marker.
explanation.zh: -(으)려고 接动词词干表示意图或目的：한국어를 배우려고 한국에 왔어요（为了学韩语来到韩国）。辅音后接 으려고，元音后接 려고。不能与时制词尾共现。

title.zh: 用estar + 副动词表示进行

explanation.en: Estar + gerundio describes an action in progress: estoy comiendo means I am eating. The gerund is regular: -ando for -ar verbs and -iendo for -er/-ir verbs, with stem changes like leyendo or durmiendo. Only estar is conjugated; the gerund never changes for person.
explanation.zh: estar + 副动词表示正在进行的动作：estoy comiendo（我正在吃）。副动词规则构成：-ar 动词用 -ando，-er/-ir 动词用 -iendo，另有 leyendo、durmiendo 等变体。只有 estar 随人称变化，副动词不变。

questions.prompt: En el progresivo, el verbo que se conjuga es ___.

title.en: Confident guesses with 一定 and 看来
title.zh: 用“一定”和“看来”表达推断

explanation.en: 一定 expresses a confident deduction: 他一定知道 means he must know. 看来 presents a guess based on what the speaker observes: 天黑了，看来要下雨了 means it looks like it will rain. 吧 can soften a guess at the end of a sentence: 你已经吃饭了吧.
explanation.zh: “一定”表示有把握的推断：他一定知道。“看来”根据所见情况作出推测：天黑了，看来要下雨了。“吧”放在句末可使猜测语气缓和：你已经吃饭了吧。

title.en: Deductions with はず and に違いない
title.zh: 用「はず」「に違いない」表达推断

explanation.en: はず marks a reasoned expectation: 彼はもう着くはずだ means he should have arrived by now. に違いない is a stronger deduction: あの店は高いに違いない means that shop must be expensive. Both follow plain-form predicates; na-adjectives take な and nouns take の before はず but join に違いない directly.
explanation.zh: 「はず」表示有依据的推测：彼はもう着くはずだ（他应该已经到了）。「に違いない」推断语气更强：あの店は高いに違いない。两者接普通形；な形容词和名词接「はず」时用「な/の」，接「に違いない」时直接连接。

examples: 彼は知っているはずです。
あの人は田中さんに違いない。

questions.prompt: あの店は高い___。（強い推測）

choices: このへんは静かにはずです。
このへんは静かだはずです。
このへんは静かなはずです。

explanation.en: -나 보다 shares a guess based on what the speaker sees or feels: 비가 오나 봐요 means it looks like rain; action verbs take -나 보다 while descriptive verbs take -(으)ㄴ가 보다. -겠 marks a conjecture about the future or an unseen situation: 맛있겠어요 means it will probably taste good.
explanation.zh: -나 보다 根据亲眼所见或感受作推测：비가 오나 봐요（好像要下雨了）；动作动词接 -나 보다，形容词接 -(으)ㄴ가 보다。-겠 对未来或未亲见的情况作推测：맛있겠어요（应该会好吃）。

title.en: Guessing with the future and deber de
title.zh: 用将来时和deber de表达推测

explanation.en: The simple future can make a guess about the present: estará en casa means he is probably at home. Deber de + infinitive gives the same idea: debe de estar en casa. Use deber + infinitive without de for obligation instead: debe estudiar means he has to study.
explanation.zh: 简单将来时可以对现在作推测：estará en casa（他大概在家）。deber de + 原形动词表达相同含义：debe de estar en casa。而 deber + 原形（不带 de）表示义务：debe estudiar（他应该学习）。

title.en: Pointing with 这 and 那

explanation.en: 这 points to something near the speaker (“this”); 那 points to something farther away (“that”). Before a noun, add the right measure word: 这个人, 那本书, 这杯水.
explanation.zh: “这”指近处的事物，“那”指远处的事物。名词前要加合适的量词：这个人、那本书、这杯水。

questions.prompt: 哪句用“这”指近处的东西？

explanation.en: 这 marks things close to the speaker; 那 marks far things and 哪 asks a question.
explanation.zh: “这”指离说话人近的东西；“那”指远处，“哪”用于提问。

explanation.en: The order is 那 + measure word + noun + 是…
explanation.zh: 语序是“那 + 量词 + 名词 + 是……”。

explanation.en: 这 can stand alone as the subject for something nearby.
explanation.zh: “这”可以单独作主语，指近处的地方或东西。

explanation.en: 那 marks distance; 本 is the measure word for books.
explanation.zh: “那”指远处；“本”是书的量词。

title.en: Point with これ・それ・あれ
title.zh: 用「これ・それ・あれ」指东西

explanation.en: Japanese uses three words for pointing: これ for things near the speaker, それ near the listener, and あれ far from both. Before a noun they become この, その, あの: この本, あの人.
explanation.zh: 日语用三个词指东西：これ（说话人近处）、それ（听话人近处）、あれ（双方都远）。修饰名词时用この・その・あの：この本、あの人。

questions.prompt: 話す人の近くにあるものを指す言葉はどれですか。

explanation.en: これ marks what is near the speaker; それ is near the listener and あれ far from both.
explanation.zh: 「これ」指说话人近处；「それ」指听话人近处；「あれ」指双方都远。

questions.prompt: 正しい文を選んでください。

explanation.en: Before a noun, これ becomes この and あれ becomes あの.
explanation.zh: 修饰名词时用「この」「あの」，不能说「これ本」「あれ人」。

explanation.en: あれ points to something far from both speaker and listener.
explanation.zh: 「あれ」指离双方都远的东西。

explanation.en: それ points to something near the listener.
explanation.zh: 「それ」指听话人近处的东西。

title.zh: 用 이・그・저 指人或物

explanation.en: Korean has three demonstratives: 이 for things near the speaker, 그 near the listener, and 저 far from both. They combine with 것 to mean “this/that thing” (이것, 그것, 저것) and go directly before nouns: 이 책, 그 사람, 저 건물.
explanation.zh: 韩语有三个指示词：이（说话人近处）、그（听话人近处）、저（双方都远）。和 것 组合成 이것/그것/저것；直接放在名词前：이 책、그 사람、저 건물。

questions.prompt: 말하는 사람 가까이 있는 것을 가리키는 말은 무엇입니까?

explanation.en: 이 marks what is near the speaker; 그 near the listener, 저 far from both.
explanation.zh: 이 指说话人近处；그 指听话人近处；저 指双方都远。

explanation.en: Before a noun use 이/그/저, not 이것/그것/저것.
explanation.zh: 名词前用 이/그/저，不能用 이것/그것/저것。

explanation.en: 저 points to something far from both speaker and listener.
explanation.zh: 저 指离双方都远的东西。

explanation.en: 그 points to something near the listener.
explanation.zh: 그 指听话人近处。

title.en: Point with este, ese and aquel

explanation.en: Spanish demonstratives change for gender and distance: este/esta for things near the speaker, ese/esa near the listener, and aquel/aquella far away. Match the noun's gender: este libro, esa mesa, aquella casa.
explanation.zh: 西班牙语指示词随性和距离变化：este/esta 指说话人近处，ese/esa 指听话人近处，aquel/aquella 指远处。词性要和名词一致：este libro、esa mesa、aquella casa。

questions.prompt: ¿Qué palabra señala algo cerca del hablante?

explanation.en: Este marks something near the speaker; ese near the listener; aquel far away.
explanation.zh: Este 指说话人近处；ese 指听话人近处；aquel 指远处。

explanation.en: Silla is feminine, so the demonstrative must be esta.
explanation.zh: Silla 是阴性，所以用 esta。

explanation.en: Ese points to something near the listener.
explanation.zh: Ese 指听话人近处的东西。

explanation.en: The house is far away and casa is feminine: aquella.
explanation.zh: 房子在远处，casa 是阴性，用 aquella。

explanation.en: 如果 introduces a condition (“if…”) and 就 marks the result (“then…”): 如果下雨，我就不去。When the context is clear, 如果 can be dropped.
explanation.zh: “如果”引出条件，“就”引出结果：如果下雨，我就不去。语境清楚时“如果”可以省略。

examples: 如果明天下雨，我就不去跑步。
如果你有时间，就给我打个电话。

explanation.en: 如果…就… links a condition to its result.
explanation.zh: “如果……就……”把条件和结果连起来。

questions.prompt: 填空：___ 天气好，我们就去公园。

explanation.en: If marks a condition; 虽然 concedes and 因为 gives a reason.
explanation.zh: 条件句用“如果”；“虽然”表转折，“因为”表原因。

choices: 如果我生病就不上班是。

explanation.en: 如果 heads the condition clause and 就 heads the result.
explanation.zh: “如果”带条件分句，“就”带结果分句。

questions.prompt: “如果太贵，我就不买”里的“就”表示 ___。

explanation.en: Here 就 introduces the result when the condition holds.
explanation.zh: 这里的“就”引出条件成立时的结果。

explanation.en: 〜たら marks a condition: 雨が降ったら、行きません (if it rains, I won't go). It is the た-form plus ら. For picking up a topic as a condition, なら is used: 行くなら、早く出よう.
explanation.zh: 「〜たら」表示条件：雨が降ったら、行きません。由た形+ら构成。「なら」用于承接话题：行くなら、早く出よう。

examples: 雨が降ったら、家にいます。
暇だったら、電話してください。
東京に行くなら、この電車です。

questions.prompt: 「雨が降ったら、行きません」の意味は___。

explanation.en: 〜たら turns the first clause into a condition.
explanation.zh: 「〜たら」把前句变成条件。

questions.prompt: 正しい文を選んでください。
choices: 暇だったら、来てください。
暇だたら、来てください。

explanation.en: 暇 is a na-adjective: 暇だ + ったら gives 暇だったら.
explanation.zh: 「暇」是な形容词：暇だ+ったら→暇だったら。

questions.prompt: 「食べたら」の「たら」は___を表します。

explanation.en: たら marks a condition, not just the past.
explanation.zh: 「たら」表条件，不只是过去。

explanation.en: 着く + たら becomes 着いたら.
explanation.zh: 着く+たら→着いたら。

explanation.en: -(으)면 attaches to a stem to mark a condition: 비가 오면 집에 있어요 (if it rains, I stay home). Use -으면 after a final consonant and -면 after a vowel: 먹으면, 가면. After a noun, -(이)면 means “if it is”: 학생이면 할인이 있어요.
explanation.zh: -(으)면 接在词干后表条件：비가 오면 집에 있어요。有收音用 -으면，无收音用 -면：먹으면、가면。名词后用 -(이)면：학생이면 할인이 있어요。

explanation.en: -(으)면 makes the first clause a condition.
explanation.zh: -(으)면 把前句变成条件。

explanation.en: Stems ending in a consonant take -으면: 먹으면.
explanation.zh: 有收音的词干接 -으면：먹으면。

explanation.en: -(으)면 marks a condition.
explanation.zh: -(으)면 表条件。

explanation.en: 가 ends in a vowel, so it takes -면: 가면.
explanation.zh: 가 无收音，接 -면：가면。

title.zh: 用 si 说真实条件

explanation.en: Si introduces a real condition in the present: Si llueve, me quedo en casa (if it rains, I stay home). After si the verb stays in the indicative, never the future or subjunctive: si tengo tiempo, te ayudo.
explanation.zh: si 引出现在时的真实条件：Si llueve, me quedo en casa。si 从句用陈述式现在时，不用将来时或虚拟式：si tengo tiempo, te ayudo。

explanation.en: Si + present marks a real, possible condition.
explanation.zh: Si+现在时表示真实可能的条件。

choices: Si tengo dinero, compro el libro.
Si tendré dinero, compro el libro.
Si tengo dinero compro libro el.

explanation.en: After si use the indicative present, not the future.
explanation.zh: si 后用陈述式现在时，不用将来时。

explanation.en: The si-clause keeps the indicative.
explanation.zh: si 从句用陈述式。

explanation.en: Si introduces the condition.
explanation.zh: si 引出条件。

title.en: Have someone do with 使/让/叫

explanation.en: 使, 让 and 叫 mark that someone causes another person to act: 老师让学生先回家 (the teacher has the students go home first). 使 is the most formal; 让 and 叫 are everyday and can also mean “to let/allow”.
explanation.zh: “使、让、叫”表示让某人做某事：老师让学生先回家。“使”最正式；“让、叫”更常用，也可表示“允许”。

questions.prompt: 哪句表示“让别人做某事”？

explanation.en: The causer comes first, then 使/让/叫 plus the person who acts.
explanation.zh: 使动者在前，“使/让/叫”后接做事的人。

explanation.en: Here 让 means “let/allow”, a common extension of the causative.
explanation.zh: 这里的“让”表示“允许”，是使役的常见引申。

choices: 这个消息使大家很担心。

explanation.en: 消息 + 使 + 大家 + 很担心 follows the causative order.
explanation.zh: “使”句的语序：原因 + 使 + 人 + 状态/动作。

questions.prompt: 填空：老师___我们先把书收起来。

explanation.en: 叫 marks the person caused to act; 被 is passive and 把 fronts the object.
explanation.zh: “叫”引出被要求做事的人；“被”表被动，“把”提前宾语。

title.en: Make or let someone do with 〜させる

explanation.en: The causative 〜させる means to make or let someone do something: 先生は学生に読ませます (the teacher has the student read). Godan verbs change the last kana to the あ-row and add せる (読ませる); ichidan verbs drop る and add させる (食べさせる). The person made to act is marked with に.
explanation.zh: 使役形「〜させる」表示让某人做某事：先生は学生に読ませます。五段动词把词尾变あ段+せる（読ませる）；一段动词去る+させる（食べさせる）。被使役的人用に。

examples: 母は私に野菜を食べさせます。
先生は学生に作文を書かせました。
部長は田中さんに報告書を作らせます。

questions.prompt: 「母は私に掃除させます」で掃除するのは___。

explanation.en: The person marked with に does the action.
explanation.zh: に 标记的人是动作执行者。

questions.prompt: 「食べる」の使役形はどれですか。

explanation.en: Ichidan verbs drop る and add させる.
explanation.zh: 一段动词去る+させる。

questions.prompt: 正しい文を選んでください。
choices: 先生は学生に歌を歌わせました。
先生は学生を歌を歌させました。
先生は学生に歌を歌せました。

explanation.en: The actor is marked に and 歌う becomes 歌わせる.
explanation.zh: 被使役者用に；歌う→歌わせる。

explanation.en: 読む → 読ま + せる (godan あ-row + せる).
explanation.zh: 読む→読ま+せる（五段あ段+せる）。

explanation.en: -게 하다 marks that someone makes or lets another person act: 선생님이 학생에게 읽게 해요 (the teacher has the student read). The person made to act is marked with 에게/한테 or 을/를. With an adjective stem it means to make something reach a state: 방을 깨끗하게 해요.
explanation.zh: -게 하다 表示让某人做某事：선생님이 학생에게 읽게 해요。被使役的人用 에게/한테 或 을/를。形容词词干+-게 하다 表示使某物达到某种状态：방을 깨끗하게 해요。

questions.prompt: 「어머니가 저에게 숙제를 하게 해요」에서 숙제하는 사람은___。

explanation.en: The person marked 에게 does the action.
explanation.zh: 에게 标记的人是动作执行者。

explanation.en: Mark the caused person with 에게 and attach -게 to the verb stem.
explanation.zh: 被使役者用 에게；动词词干接 -게。

explanation.en: -게 하다 expresses making or letting someone do.
explanation.zh: -게 하다 表示让/使某人做。

explanation.en: Adjective stem + -게 하다 means causing a state.
explanation.zh: 形容词词干+-게 하다 表示使……达到某状态。

title.en: Have someone do with hacer + infinitive
title.zh: 用 hacer + 不定式说使役

explanation.en: Hacer + infinitive means to have or make someone do something: El profesor hace leer el texto a los alumnos. The person who performs the action is introduced with a or used as a direct object. With dejar instead of hacer, it means to let: Dejo salir al gato.
explanation.zh: hacer + 不定式表示让某人做某事：El profesor hace leer el texto a los alumnos。执行动作的人用 a 引出或作直接宾语。dejar + 不定式表示允许：Dejo salir al gato。

examples: El jefe hace trabajar al equipo los sábados.
Mi madre me hace estudiar dos horas.

questions.prompt: «La madre hace limpiar la habitación al niño»: ¿quién limpia?

explanation.en: The person after a (or the object pronoun) performs the action.
explanation.zh: a 后的人（或宾语代词）是动作执行者。

choices: El profesor hace leer a los alumnos.
El profesor hace leyendo a los alumnos.
El profesor hace a leer los alumnos.

explanation.en: Hacer is followed directly by the infinitive.
explanation.zh: hacer 后直接接不定式。

explanation.en: Dejar + infinitive expresses permission, not obligation.
explanation.zh: dejar + 不定式表示允许，不表强迫。

explanation.en: The causative structure is hacer + infinitive.
explanation.zh: 使役结构是 hacer + 不定式。

explanation.en: Clock time uses 点 for o'clock and 分 for minutes: 三点二十分 (3:20). Dates go from big to small: 五月十二号 (May 12). Weekdays use 星期 + number: 星期三; Sunday is 星期天/星期日.
explanation.zh: 钟点用“点”和“分”：三点二十分。日期从大到小：五月十二号。星期用“星期+数字”：星期三；星期日是星期天。

examples: 今天是八月三号，星期四。

explanation.en: 三点 is 3 o'clock and 二十分 is 20 minutes.
explanation.zh: 三点是三时，二十分是二十分钟。

explanation.en: Dates go month then day: 七月十号.
explanation.zh: 日期先说月后说日：七月十号。

explanation.en: 星期 + 三 means Wednesday, the third weekday counted.
explanation.zh: “星期+三”是星期三。

explanation.en: Only a weekday fits “我们休息”.
explanation.zh: 只有星期几才能接“我们休息”。

explanation.en: Hours use 時 and minutes 分: 三時二十分 (3:20); 半 means half past. Days of the week end in 曜日: 月曜日 to 日曜日. Dates say the month first: 四月五日. Ask with 何時, 何曜日, 何日.
explanation.zh: 时间用「時」和「分」：三時二十分；「半」是半点。星期以「曜日」结尾：月曜日〜日曜日。日期先说月：四月五日。提问用何時・何曜日・何日。

examples: 五月三日に会いましょう。

explanation.en: 半 means half past the hour.
explanation.zh: 「半」是半点。

questions.prompt: 正しい文を選んでください。

explanation.en: Weekdays end in 曜日 and take は after the topic.
explanation.zh: 星期以「曜日」结尾，主题后用は。

explanation.en: 何曜日 asks the day of the week.
explanation.zh: 「何曜日」问星期几。

explanation.en: A day expression fits before a date; 時 is clock time.
explanation.zh: 日期前用「明日」等日子词；「時」是钟点。

explanation.en: Korean tells time with native numbers for hours and Sino-Korean numbers for minutes: 세 시 이십오 분 (3:25); 반 is half past. Days end in 요일: 월요일 to 일요일; dates say 월 then 일: 오월 십일. Ask with 몇 시, 무슨 요일, 며칠.
explanation.zh: 韩语钟点用固有数词+시，分钟用汉字数词+분：세 시 이십오 분；반 是半点。星期以요일结尾：월요일〜일요일；日期월+일：오월 십일。提问用 몇 시、무슨 요일、며칠。

explanation.en: 반 means half past.
explanation.zh: 반 是半点。

explanation.en: 요일 names the weekday with 은/는 as topic.
explanation.zh: 星期名以요일结尾，用은/는。

explanation.en: 며칠 asks the day of the month (the date).
explanation.zh: 며칠 问几号（日期）。

explanation.en: Hours use native numbers (한/두/세 시); minutes use Sino numbers.
explanation.zh: 钟点用固有数词（한/두/세 시）；分钟用汉字数词。

explanation.en: Ask ¿Qué hora es? and answer es la una for one o'clock, son las + number otherwise: son las tres y veinte (3:20); y media is half past, menos cuarto is quarter to. Days and months take small letters: lunes, enero. Dates use el + day + de + month: el cinco de mayo.
explanation.zh: 问时间用 ¿Qué hora es?；一点用 es la una，其余用 son las+数字：son las tres y veinte；y media 是半点，menos cuarto 是差一刻。星期和月份小写：lunes、enero。日期用 el+日+de+月：el cinco de mayo。

examples: Mi cumpleaños es el ocho de junio.

explanation.en: Y cuarto adds fifteen minutes.
explanation.zh: y cuarto 是过一刻（15分）。

explanation.en: “Today is Tuesday” takes no article: hoy es martes.
explanation.zh: “今天是周二”不用冠词：hoy es martes。

questions.prompt: «Es la una y media» usa «es» porque ___.

explanation.en: Only la una is singular; other hours take son.
explanation.zh: 只有 la una 是单数，其余钟点用 son。

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi examen es ___ diez de abril.

explanation.en: Dates take the article el: el diez de abril.
explanation.zh: 日期前用冠词 el：el diez de abril。

explanation.en: Put a verb phrase before 的 to modify a noun: 昨天买的书 (the book bought yesterday), 我喜欢的人 (the person I like). The modified noun follows 的; the describing clause comes first, the opposite order to English.
explanation.zh: 把动词短语放在“的”前面修饰名词：昨天买的书、我喜欢的人。被修饰的名词在“的”后面，顺序和英语相反。

explanation.en: 昨天买 describes 书 through 的.
explanation.zh: “昨天买”通过“的”修饰“书”。

explanation.en: The 的-clause precedes the noun it modifies.
explanation.zh: “的”字短语在被修饰名词之前。

questions.prompt: 填空：在图书馆工作___人是我的老师。

explanation.en: 的 links the describing clause 在图书馆工作 to 人.
explanation.zh: “的”连接修饰语“在图书馆工作”和“人”。

explanation.en: 他做 describes 菜; he is the one who cooks.
explanation.zh: “他做”修饰“菜”，做菜的是“他”。

explanation.en: A plain-form clause before a noun describes it: 昨日買った本 (the book bought yesterday), 読んでいる人 (a person who is reading). No particle like の is needed between the clause and the noun.
explanation.zh: 普通形短句直接放在名词前修饰它：昨日買った本、読んでいる人。短句和名词之间不加「の」。

examples: 昨日買った本は面白いです。
駅にいる人は友達です。

explanation.en: 昨日買った describes 本; the plain-form clause precedes the noun.
explanation.zh: 「昨日買った」修饰「本」，普通形短句在名词前。

questions.prompt: 正しい文を選んでください。
choices: 読んでいる人は姉です。
読んでいるの人は姉です。
人読んでいるは姉です。

explanation.en: No の is needed between the clause and the noun.
explanation.zh: 短句和名词之间不加「の」。

questions.prompt: 「私が作ったケーキ」で作ったのは___。

explanation.en: 私が作った describes ケーキ; the maker is 私.
explanation.zh: 「私が作った」修饰「ケーキ」，做的人是「私」。

explanation.en: A plain-form clause 病院にいる modifies 人.
explanation.zh: 普通形「病院にいる」修饰「人」。

explanation.en: Verb and adjective stems take adnominal endings before a noun: 먹은 사과 (the apple that was eaten), 읽는 사람 (a person who reads), 먹을 책 (a book to read). Use -(으)ㄴ for completed/past, -는 for present, -(으)ㄹ for future: 만난 친구, 만나는 친구, 만날 친구.
explanation.zh: 动词、形容词词干在名词前接冠形词尾：먹은 사과、읽는 사람、먹을 책。已发生用 -(으)ㄴ，进行用 -는，将来用 -(으)ㄹ：만난 친구、만나는 친구、만날 친구。

explanation.en: 산 (past adnominal of 사다) describes 책.
explanation.zh: 산（사다 的过去冠形）修饰 책。

explanation.en: Present action takes -는: 자는 아이.
explanation.zh: 进行中的动作用 -는：자는 아이。

explanation.en: -(으)ㄹ marks a future modifier.
explanation.zh: -(으)ㄹ 表示将来的修饰。

explanation.en: Adjective stems take -(으)ㄴ to modify nouns: 예쁜.
explanation.zh: 形容词词干接 -(으)ㄴ 修饰名词：예쁜。

title.zh: 用 que 从句修饰名词

explanation.en: Use que to attach a clause to a noun: el libro que compré (the book that I bought), la persona que vive aquí (the person who lives here). Unlike English, que cannot be dropped: la casa que vendió (the house she sold).
explanation.zh: 用 que 把从句接在名词后：el libro que compré、la persona que vive aquí。与英语不同，que 不能省略：la casa que vendió。

examples: El libro que compré es interesante.
La chica que canta es mi hermana.
La casa que ves es antigua.

explanation.en: Que compré describes el libro.
explanation.zh: que compré 修饰 el libro。

choices: La persona que canta es Ana.
La persona canta es Ana que.
La que persona canta es Ana.

explanation.en: The que-clause follows the noun it describes.
explanation.zh: que 从句在被修饰名词之后。

questions.prompt: «La película que vimos» — ¿quién vio la película?

explanation.en: Que vimos means “that we saw”.
explanation.zh: que vimos 是“我们看的”。

questions.prompt: Completa: El coche ___ compraste es rojo.

explanation.en: Que links the clause to the noun.
explanation.zh: que 连接从句和名词。

title.en: Report what others say with 据说 and 听说

explanation.en: 据说 and 听说 report information heard from others without vouching for it: 据说这家店很有名 (it's said this shop is famous), 听说他辞职了 (I heard he quit). 据说 is more formal; both distance the speaker from the claim, unlike directly stating facts.
explanation.zh: “据说”“听说”表示转述从别处听到的信息，说话人不为真实性担保：据说这家店很有名、听说他辞职了。“据说”更正式；两者都与直接陈述事实不同。

questions.prompt: “据说这家店很有名”的意思是 ___。

explanation.en: 据说 reports what others say, not the speaker's own claim.
explanation.zh: “据说”表示转述别人的话，不是说话人自己的断言。

explanation.en: 听说 introduces the reported clause.
explanation.zh: “听说”引出转述的内容。

explanation.en: Both report hearsay; 据说 is the more formal/written choice.
explanation.zh: 都表转述；“据说”更正式，多用于书面。

questions.prompt: 填空：___ 明天的考试取消了，大家都在讨论。

explanation.en: The clause is reported information, so 听说 fits; 一定 asserts, 难道 questions.
explanation.zh: 句中是转述消息，用“听说”；“一定”表断定，“难道”表反问。

title.en: Report hearsay with 〜そうだ and らしい
title.zh: 用「〜そうだ」「らしい」转述传闻

explanation.en: 〜そうだ after a plain form reports hearsay: 明日雨が降るそうだ (they say it will rain). らしい also marks information heard indirectly, with a slight guess: 彼は来ないらしい. Do not confuse hearsay そうだ with the looks-like そうだ (おいしそう).
explanation.zh: 普通形+「〜そうだ」表示传闻：明日雨が降るそうだ。「らしい」也表间接听到的信息并带推测：彼は来ないらしい。注意传闻「そうだ」与样态「そうだ」（おいしそう）不同。

examples: あの店はおいしいそうです。
田中さんは来ないらしいです。
明日は雪が降るそうです。

questions.prompt: 「あの店はおいしいそうです」の意味は___。

explanation.en: そうだ here reports hearsay, not appearance.
explanation.zh: 这里的「そうだ」表传闻，不是样态。

questions.prompt: 正しい文を選んでください。
choices: 彼は来ないそうだです。
彼は来ないのそうです。

explanation.en: Plain form + そうだ; polite speech adds です after そう.
explanation.zh: 普通形+そうだ；礼貌体在そう后加です。

questions.prompt: 「おいしそう」と「おいしいそうだ」の違いは___。

explanation.en: おいしそう (looks tasty) is appearance; おいしいそうだ reports hearsay.
explanation.zh: 「おいしそう」是样子，「おいしいそうだ」是传闻。

explanation.en: 休みだ + そうです → 休みだそうです.
explanation.zh: 休みだ+そうです→休みだそうです。

explanation.en: -(ㄴ)대요 reports what someone else said: 비가 온대요 (they say it will rain / I heard it rains). The ending changes by stem type: verbs take -ㄴ대요/-는대요 (간대요/먹는대요), adjectives -대요 (좋대요), and 이다 becomes -(이)래요 (학생이래요).
explanation.zh: -(ㄴ)대요 表示转述别人的话：비가 온대요。动词词干接 -ㄴ대요/-는대요（간대요/먹는대요），形容词接 -대요（좋대요），이다 变成 -(이)래요（학생이래요）。

explanation.en: -(ㄴ)대요 relays what the speaker heard.
explanation.zh: -(ㄴ)대요 转述听来的内容。

explanation.en: Vowel-ending verb stems take -ㄴ대요: 가+ㄴ대요 → 간대요.
explanation.zh: 无收音动词词干接 -ㄴ대요：가+ㄴ대요→간대요。

explanation.en: 이다 + indirect quote ending gives -(이)래요.
explanation.zh: 이다+间接引用结尾→-(이)래요。

explanation.en: Adjective stems take -대요: 맛있+대요.
explanation.zh: 形容词词干接 -대요：맛있+대요。

title.en: Report what people say with dicen que and según
title.zh: 用 dicen que 和 según 转述传闻

explanation.en: Dicen que reports what people say: dicen que llueve mañana (they say it rains tomorrow). Según marks the source: según el diario, la tienda cierra (according to the paper, the shop closes). Reported speech keeps the indicative: dijo que venía (he said he was coming).
explanation.zh: dicen que 转述众人的说法：dicen que llueve mañana。según 标明来源：según el diario。转述时动词保持陈述式：dijo que venía。

examples: Dicen que la película es buena.
Según el mapa, el banco está cerca.

questions.prompt: «Dicen que la película es buena» significa ___.

explanation.en: Dicen que reports what others say.
explanation.zh: dicen que 转述别人的说法。

explanation.en: Reported speech needs que after dijo.
explanation.zh: 转述时 dijo 后需要 que。

explanation.en: Según introduces the source of the information.
explanation.zh: según 引出信息来源。

questions.prompt: «Dicen que llueve» usa el verbo en ___.

explanation.en: Reported clauses keep the indicative.
explanation.zh: 转述从句用陈述式。
